why: Each row has the three wing types (two-pointed, many-feathered, plain) and the three bellies (black, hatched, white), and each pair goes together: two-pointed wings with a black belly, many-feathered wings with a hatched belly, plain wings with a white belly. Row 3 already has many-feathered/hatched and plain/white, so the missing bird is two-pointed wings with a half-black belly: option 1. Option 6 has a fully black belly, which is not used in the grid. Options 2, 3, 4 and 5 have the wrong wing type or belly.
trick: Count wing types and belly shadings in each row; the missing cell takes the one wing type and one shading not yet used.
note: The book key prints 3 (plain wings, hatched belly), but row 3 already has a hatched belly and plain wings, so it cannot be right. Answer set to 1 by the row rule.
